title: A Postcard for the Orchard Anew
premise: Marguerite Kavanagh has spent a decade training her heart like any other muscle—disciplined, contained, never overworked. When a blizzard traps her in a mountain inn with Julian Reyes, the rival pâtissier who broke her heart at twenty-four, and Theo Lindqvist, the investor deciding her café's fate, old wounds and new stakes collide: the two men were once best friends, and their falling-out was about her. As debts close in, Marguerite must choose between the safe survival of keeping everyone at arm's length and risking everything on love she once swore off. In the end, she loses the café but wins back herself, opening a small orchard-side bakery with Julian while Theo, finally forgiven, becomes her business partner instead of her owner.
about_author: Ines Zhou is a former line cook who traded kitchen shifts for manuscript pages after a decade of feeding strangers in three countries. She writes romances about people who are better with recipes than with feelings.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A final notice arrives at Butter & Bloom café the same week her landlord doubles the rent; she responds by perfecting an orchard-plum tart no one ordered. Her ex-mentor warns that pride is expensive. Emotional beat: controlled panic masked as competence, establishing her creed that hearts, like ovens, should run hot only under supervision.

chapters.title: The Investor Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Theo Lindqvist appears at her counter unannounced, offering rescue capital with unsettling familiarity—he already knows her signature pastry, her mother's name, her failure at Le Cordon Bleu. She signs nothing but accepts his invitation to a due-diligence weekend at his inn. Beat: unease dressed as opportunity; the reader senses he knows more than he says.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, shifting to Julian's at midpoint. The storm hits early; stranded guests include Julian Reyes, now a celebrated chef whose cookbook she owns and resents. Their first meeting in ten years is witnessed by Theo, who goes pale. Beat: shock and old fury reigniting; Julian recognizes her instantly, and the past walks into the room wearing snow.

chapters.title: What Happened in Lyon
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Flashback woven through present: in culinary school, Julian and Theo were inseparable until both loved Marguerite, and Julian let Theo believe a lie to win her—then vanished before she could choose. Now snowbound, they circle each other with knives wrapped in politeness. Beat: guilt exposed; the reader learns the rivalry was engineered by cowardice, not passion.

chapters.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Trapped together for days, the trio cooks one meal after another; Marguerite teaches Julian her plum tart, and muscle memory betrays them into tenderness. Theo watches, saying little. She catches herself laughing and hates it. Beat: warmth thawing armor; desire returning like feeling to a numb limb—painful and proof of life.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals his investment offer is contingent: buy the café, rebrand it, keep Marguerite on as head chef—or lose it entirely. Privately, he admits to himself the deal was designed to put him near her again. Julian confronts him. Beat: love curdling into control; the price of survival made literal, and Marguerite's autonomy becoming collateral.

chapters.title: The Lie That Built Two Careers
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Cornered by the storm's last night, Julian confesses to Marguerite: he told Theo she'd chosen him, then fled before either could test the truth—and built a career on running. Marguerite realizes both men spent ten years orbiting a decision she was never allowed to make. Beat: rage and grief; the betrayal reframed as theft of her own story.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Roads clear; Theo expects her signature. Instead she pitches her own plan—an orchard bakery partnership on equal terms, no ownership of her heart included—and gives Theo an ultimatum: invest as a friend or not at all. He walks out. Beat: climax of agency; she risks the whole heart and the whole business rather than lending pieces.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Marguerite and Theo. The café goes to auction; at the last minute Theo outbids the developer—then deeds half to Marguerite and half to Julian, asking forgiveness instead of terms. Julian offers partnership, not possession. Beat: resolution of power; love demonstrated by release, the debt paid in humility rather than money.

chapters.title: Postcard from the Orchard
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue in spring. One year later: the Orchard Anew bakery opens among blooming trees, co-run with Julian, with Theo's name on the letterhead and a standing Sunday table. Marguerite mails a postcard to her younger self: the heart survived. Beat: belonging earned, identity whole—love as something grown, not guarded.
